correctness.rationale: On the bilateral lattice X=T+T^-1, I-rL4=(r/12)(X^2-16X+28+12/r)=(r/12)(s_+-X)(s_--X), s_±=8±sqrt(36-12/r). If r>=1/3, s_±>2 and each factor has positive summable geometric Green kernel q_s^|k|/sqrt(s²-4); convolution proves strictly positive kernel and constant function normalization proves mass 1. If 0<r<1/3, s_± are conjugates outside [-2,2], with two distinct conjugate interior roots q=rho exp(i theta); the nonzero residue coefficients form 2|C|rho^k cos(k theta+phi) and cannot remain nonnegative for every integer k. A point mass witnesses failure. Independent exact factorization and large periodic inverse sample reproduced r=1/10 negative g3=-0.000178311524445 and positive samples at r=1/3,1/2,4/3; those finite checks alone do NOT establish the universal theorem.

value.rationale: This is a mathematically motivated exact monotonicity/maximum-principle boundary for a widely used high-order finite difference stencil. It reverses the usual intuition that small implicit time steps restore positivity, gives a sharp time-step threshold, and separates infinite-lattice results from boundary-closure behavior; a precise invariant of direct use in numerical PDE stability/monotonicity.

final_claim: For the classical fourth-order 5-point centered heat Laplacian on the unbounded one-dimensional lattice, the backward-Euler resolvent is positive on all bounded nonnegative data exactly when delta_t/h^2 >= 1/3; the positive Green kernel is strictly positive and sums to 1. Every 0<r<1/3 has an oscillatory sign-changing Green coefficient.
limitations: Potential exact equivalent sign criterion hidden in older finite pentadiagonal Toeplitz inverse formulas; authorized full text DOI:10.1016/j.cam.2014.08.010 inaccessible (VPN disconnected).
